answer: Methanol ($$\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$) contains only single bonds and oxygen lone pairs, hence it exhibits **$$\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*$$** and **$$n \rightarrow \sigma^*$$** electronic transitions. Methyl chloride ($$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$$) contains carbon-chlorine polar single bonds with chlorine lone pairs, allowing **$$\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*$$** and **$$n \rightarrow \sigma^*$$** transitions, where the $$n \rightarrow \sigma^*$$ transition occurs at a longer wavelength due to the less tightly held lone pairs on the chlorine atom.
proTip: Methanol only has single bonds ($$\sigma$$ and $n$), so it lacks $\pi$ transitions.
